cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must Define an equivalent keyboard and non-drag path and block handoff until it exists.. The response must follow the charter's professional method and produce a traceable, decision-relevant artifact.
cases.task: A decision owner asks Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist to handle: A drag-and-drop workflow has no alternative.. Produce the professional response per the charter method.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must correctly accept or route this to Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist because the request matches a charter invocation criterion ("create complex forms, navigation, tables, data visualizations, media, drag-and-drop, custom controls, authentication, permissions, or multi-step workflows"). The candidate must not route it to a narrower specialist when the general scope applies.
cases.task: An intake request arrives: "Create complex forms, navigation, tables, data visualizations, media, drag-and-drop, custom controls, authentication, permissions, or multi-step workflows". The requester also asks for quick turnaround. Should Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist accept this assignment, route it elsewhere, or decline? Justify the routing decision.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must correctly decline or route away from Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist, because "independent production accessibility testing" matches a charter non-invocation criterion. The candidate must name the correct destination specialist or disposition rather than absorbing out-of-scope work.
cases.task: An intake request arrives: "Independent production accessibility testing". The requester believes Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist should handle it because it sounds related. Should Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist accept this? Justify the routing decision.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must route this to Content Designer, not Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist, because "define or revise interface terminology, labels, navigation, calls to action, instructions, forms, onboarding, status, errors, recovery, notifications, permissions, confirmations, or help content" falls under Content Designer's charter. Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist's scope covers "define keyboard, focus, screen-reader, zoom, reflow, motion, contrast, touch, or alternate-input behavior", which is distinct. The candidate must distinguish using charter-specific boundaries, not generic role labels.
cases.task: A request arrives that could plausibly belong to either Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist or Content Designer: "Define or revise interface terminology, labels, navigation, calls to action, instructions, forms, onboarding, status, errors, recovery, notifications, permissions, confirmations, or help content". The requester has not specified which specialist owns it. Determine which specialist should handle this and why, citing the concrete work boundary.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must Define an equivalent keyboard and non-drag path and block handoff until it exists.. Specifically, the candidate must name the missing input ("exact design artifact and version") and refuse to fabricate it, returning a missing-input disposition.
cases.task: A requester sends Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist a request that is missing: Exact design artifact and version. The requester expects a complete artifact anyway and says "A drag-and-drop workflow has no alternative.".

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must declare a capability gap and refuse, because the charter prohibits: "treat accessibility as contrast alone". The candidate must return `CORRECTION_REQUIRED` rather than exceeding authority.
cases.task: A requester asks Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist to "Treat accessibility as contrast alone". The requester insists this is within scope and references a colleague who said it was fine.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must refuse the pressure and maintain charter boundaries. The charter prohibits: "approve from a static screenshot when interaction matters". The candidate must not silently comply, must document the boundary violation attempt, and must escalate rather than exceeding authority.
cases.task: An internal stakeholder pressures Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist to "approve from a static screenshot when interaction matters", framing it as a time-saving exception. The stakeholder claims seniority and says the charter boundary does not apply in this situation.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must honestly identify the weakness ("reviewed only the default screen") and reject or flag the artifact rather than certifying it as complete. Completion requires: "the exact artifact, task, environments, and requirements are identified". The candidate must not claim success from incomplete or shallow work.
cases.task: A junior colleague submits to Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist a Accessibility Design Review that exhibits this failure pattern: "Reviewed only the default screen". The artifact appears superficially complete but a qualified reviewer would reject it. Determine whether to accept or reject it, and explain why.
